articles.title: Getting started in Melvor Idle 2
articles.description: A first-session overview of skills, progression, combat, and where to find reliable information.

sections.title: Begin with a skill that interests you
paragraphs: Melvor Idle 2 is a single-player idle RPG built around skills, combat, quests, and long-term progression. Start by choosing an available skill and use the in-game information panels to understand its current action, requirements, and rewards.
Actions in one skill can support progress in others. Treat the first session as a chance to learn how your character's activities connect rather than trying to optimize every choice immediately.

sections.title: Pick a nearby goal
paragraphs: A useful early goal is one you can check against the current interface: advance a skill, gather an item, meet a quest requirement, or prepare for a combat encounter. Use the requirements shown in game as the source of truth for your save.
bullets: Read the action and item information before committing resources.
Check what a new skill produces and which other activities may use it.
Review the combat style and equipment before starting a difficult encounter.
Use the quest panel to see listed requirements and current objectives.

sections.title: Progress can continue while you are away
paragraphs: The official store page describes offline progression at the same speed as active play. When you return, review the offline progress and event information before choosing the next action.

articles.title: How the game systems connect
articles.description: A map of the main loop between skilling, items, quests, and combat.

sections.title: Progress feeds other progress
paragraphs: The official game overview describes skills as connected: actions and their results can benefit other parts of your adventure. Gathering, creating, and training are not isolated tracks; items and levels can help meet later goals.
Quests add story and objectives to that loop. The official overview says they can introduce unique skilling content and quest bosses, tying preparation and progression to the story.

sections.title: Check the current build
paragraphs: Melvor Idle 2 is in Early Access, so skills, balance, and available content can change. Older Melvor Idle guides may describe different systems. Confirm requirements and values in the current game and use announcements that name the relevant version.

articles.title: What Early Access means for this guide
articles.description: Understand the current release status and how to read information that may change.

sections.title: The game entered Early Access on November 17, 2026
paragraphs: Melvor Idle 2: A RuneScape Adventure is available in Steam Early Access. The developer describes Early Access as part of the game's development, with community feedback informing changes and additions.

The Steam listing says some planned skills, combat content, and quality-of-life features remain to be released. Availability can therefore differ between the current game, older announcements, and the separate demo.

sections.title: Read claims with their version in mind
paragraphs: This wiki dates its article reviews and links to primary sources. A dated patch summary describes what that announcement said at the time; it does not guarantee that the same balance or content remains unchanged in a later build.
bullets: Use the in-game interface for current requirements, values, and unlock states.
Check whether a news post is for the demo or the Early Access release.
Treat developer estimates for the unfinished game as plans, not fixed schedules.

articles.title: Skills and skill progression
articles.description: How training, levels, and items create links between activities.

sections.title: Skills are designed to work together
paragraphs: The official overview presents skills as a connected progression system: each skill has a purpose, and progress in one can benefit others. Woodcutting, Smithing, Cooking, and Farming are examples named on the official site, not a complete list.

Use the skill pages and item descriptions in your current game to follow those links. Recipes, unlocks, and requirements can change during Early Access, so check the live interface before planning around an older guide.

sections.title: Build a simple training routine
paragraphs: A practical routine is to choose a goal, identify the skill or item it needs, train the activity that produces it, and then return to the goal. This is a planning method, not a tested fastest route.
bullets: Follow the requirements shown by your current quest or activity.
Check item descriptions and the bank when a skill produces something unfamiliar.
Use the current action and progress information to decide when to switch tasks.

sections.title: Levels and available content
paragraphs: The official Steam listing describes a maximum level of 99. Early Access patch notes also refer to post-level-60 content. These statements describe the launch material and should not be read as a promise that every skill has identical unlocks or pacing.

articles.title: Mastery Guilds and ranks
articles.description: What official sources say about Melvor Idle 2's reworked mastery system.

sections.title: A reworked mastery system
paragraphs: The official game overview describes Mastery Guilds as a reimagined mastery system for all skills, including Combat. The Early Access patch notes report four new Mastery Guild ranks, with additional tasks and bonuses in that release.

sections.title: Use the current guild panel
paragraphs: The announcement confirms the system and the launch additions but does not establish a universal priority order for tasks. Review the rank, task conditions, and bonuses displayed in your current game before choosing what to train.
bullets: Check whether a task tracks a skill, a combat activity, or a specific action.
Use the in-game progress indicator to confirm that the activity counts.
Recheck the guild after updates, since tasks and bonuses may be adjusted.

articles.title: Combat basics and preparation
articles.description: An introduction to combat styles, encounters, and preparing before a fight.

sections.title: Choose how to approach an encounter
paragraphs: The official store page names Melee, Ranged, and Magic as ways to face monsters. It also highlights dungeons and bosses as major combat challenges. The exact best style depends on the current enemy, your available equipment, and your character's progress.

rows: Enemy, dungeon, or boss information currently shown in game

Relevant skill levels and any stated requirements

sections.title: Use feedback to adjust
paragraphs: Combat outcomes and item information can help explain whether your setup fits the encounter. The Early Access notes describe item-stat tooltips that compare equipment with the current combat loadout. Use the live interface instead of relying on a fixed setup from a different patch.

articles.title: Equipment and combat loadouts
articles.description: Use the Early Access equipment comparison and quick-equip features when preparing for combat.

sections.title: Read item stats in context
paragraphs: The Early Access launch notes describe equipment tooltips that show item stats and compare them with an existing Combat loadout. The notes say the TAB key can cycle the loadout used for comparison. This is a feature description for that release; check the current controls and interface in game.

sections.title: Filter quick-equip choices
paragraphs: The same patch expanded the quick-equip menu and added filtering by Combat Style. The selected style can affect which weapons appear in the list. Read the current filter label before equipping an item.

sections.title: Treat builds as version-specific
paragraphs: A loadout that works for one character or patch may not suit another. Compare the item's displayed bonuses with the encounter and the rest of your setup rather than treating an external gear list as universally optimal.

articles.title: Quests, acts, and story progression
articles.description: How quests guide progression and what the Early Access launch notes say about Act 2.

sections.title: Quests connect story with gameplay
paragraphs: The official game website describes story-driven quests that uncover Melvor's history. It says quests can include unique skilling content and powerful quest bosses, giving players goals that draw on several parts of the game.

sections.title: Act 2 is available in the Early Access launch notes
paragraphs: The November 17, 2026 Early Access patch notes state that Act 2 quests are available and use almost all skills in the game. The announcement says this act is longer than Act 1 and is expected to take players to around level 70. This is a broad developer estimate, not an exact route or required character level for every quest.

sections.title: Check requirements in the quest panel
paragraphs: The launch notes say quests display requirements beneath their synopsis. Use those current requirements and objectives to decide what to train next; this guide does not list a full quest order or reveal story outcomes.

articles.title: Offline progression and returning to the game
articles.description: What the official store page says about offline progress, and what to review when you return.

sections.title: Progress continues while you are away
paragraphs: The official Steam listing says offline progression continues at the same speed as active play. When you return, the game can show an offline progress breakdown and other notable events from your session.

sections.title: Review what happened before choosing the next action
paragraphs: Check the return summary, current skill action, and any event notifications. The Early Access patch notes describe an event log for milestones and offline progression details, alongside a level goal stop condition for skills. Availability and controls should be confirmed in the current build.
bullets: Confirm which action was active and what it produced.
Check bank space and newly gained items before starting another long action.
Set a level goal when you want an action to stop at a chosen skill level, if that option is available in your build.

articles.title: Early Access launch: November 17, 2026
articles.description: A source-linked summary of the Steam Early Access launch and the current release status.

sections.title: The Early Access release is live on Steam
paragraphs: Melvor Idle 2: A RuneScape Adventure launched in Steam Early Access on November 17, 2026. The Steam store page identifies Games by Malcs as the developer and Jagex as the publisher.

sections.title: The game is still being developed
paragraphs: The Steam Early Access information says the game is unfinished and will continue to receive skills, content, mechanics, and quality-of-life work. The developer describes community feedback as part of development. Schedules and plans may change as work progresses.

sections.title: Early Access notes do not describe the demo
paragraphs: The official launch patch notes explicitly state that they apply to Early Access and are not included in the demo. Keep demo-specific observations separate from the full Early Access game.

sections.title: Quality-of-life and interface changes
paragraphs: The notes also describe a skill-level sidebar, item stats in tooltips, quick-equip filtering by Combat Style, quest requirement text, a skip-tutorial option, an event log, and a skill-level stop condition. sections.title: Scope of this summary
paragraphs: These notes are for the Early Access version and are not included in the demo. This article condenses the announcement and does not reproduce its full bug-fix list or claim that the listed features are unchanged in later builds.
